sections.h2: Where is Mauldin, SC, and what is around it?
sections.html:
Mauldin is a city in Greenville County, South Carolina, south of the county's center and between Greenville to the northwest and Simpsonville to the southeast. It is part of the Greenville-Anderson-Greer metropolitan area.

The city covers about 12.13 square miles, almost all of it land, at an elevation of about 906 feet. U.S. Route 276 (Main Street) runs through the center, 8 miles to Greenville and 5 miles to Simpsonville. Interstate 385 follows the eastern side of the city, north to Interstate 85 and south to Interstate 185, and I-185 continues about 13 miles west-northwest to I-85 on the southwest side of Greenville.

Because Mauldin sits entirely in Greenville County, the county handles the assessment, the tax bill and the deed recording. That keeps a sale simpler than in neighboring Greer, which is split between two counties.

sections.h2: What is the history of Mauldin?
sections.html:
Mauldin takes its name from a railroad. Benjamin Griffith received the first land grant in the area in 1784, and in 1885 Lieutenant Governor W. L. Mauldin helped bring the Greenville and Laurens Railroad through the village. The station was named Mauldin, and the name spread to the surrounding community.

The Civil War left the community nearly depopulated, and it did not fully recover until after World War II. The city's population was 22,889 in 2010 and 24,724 in the 2020 Census, which made it the 19th most populous city in South Carolina. The Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 31,465.

That jump from 2020 to the 2025 estimate points to steady demand for housing in the area, though an estimate says nothing about the value of your house.

Mauldin is part of the Greenville metro economy, and retail and commercial development have a visible presence. The supermarket chain BI-LO was founded in Mauldin and was headquartered there until 2011. BridgeWay Station, a 400,000 square foot mixed-use development, opened in 2024.

We could not confirm a current list of Mauldin's largest employers from an official page, so we leave one out. What we can say is that the city's location along US 276 and I-385 puts residents within reach of jobs in Greenville and Simpsonville.

Public schools are run by the Greenville County School District, which operates Mauldin High School, and the Greenville County Library System has a branch in the city.

sections.h2: What permits and licenses does the City of Mauldin require?
sections.html:
The City of Mauldin issues building and zoning permits through its Business and Development Services office. The city's permit page lists forms for new residential construction, residential additions and accessory structures, decks, roofs, demolition, trades work and floodplain development, along with a zoning permit, a temporary use permit and an encroachment permit.

If you are repairing before a sale, the roof and deck permits are the ones most owners need. The city accepts cash, check and credit cards, and a single fee schedule PDF covers the fees. The page does not list amounts, so ask the office.

A business license is required for every business in or doing business in Mauldin. A new business pays a $15 review fee and a home occupation pays $25, and renewals are due April 30. If you run a home business from the house you are selling, tell the buyer, because the license does not travel with the property. Business and Development Services is at (864) 234-3475.

We did not find a city page covering rental registration or code enforcement for Mauldin, so ask the city office about open violations or rental requirements on your address.

sections.h2: How do Greenville County taxes work for a Mauldin house?
sections.html:
Mauldin owners pay property tax to Greenville County, and a sale changes the next owner's valuation. County Real Property Services lists these dates: taxes are due January 15, which is also the last day to appeal the previous year's value, and bills are typically mailed near the end of October.

Assessment notices for new construction and increased values, such as after a transfer, usually go out in late summer or early fall with a 90 day appeal window. Deeds signed on or before December 31 take effect for the next year's taxes, so the county advises recording soon after signing. The county says 2025 was a reassessment year.

A qualifying sale is an assessable transfer of interest. Greenville County reassesses the property at current market value as of December 31 of the year of the sale, and the old 15% cap no longer applies. The county's 4% owner-occupied rate requires an application, due January 15 and postmarked or hand-delivered by then. Under state law, an owner who is later ineligible faces the 6% ratio, plus a penalty of 100% of the tax paid with 0.5% monthly interest.

State law also sets a 3% penalty after January 15, another 7% after February 1 and another 5% after March 16. Settle any unpaid balance before closing so it does not become a title problem.

sections.h2: How are deeds recorded in Greenville County?
sections.html:
Mauldin deeds are recorded at the Greenville County Register of Deeds in Suite S-2100 of Greenville County Square, 301 University Ridge, Greenville. The office is open weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., and in-person recording should be done before 4:30 p.m. The phone number is 864-467-7240.

The office scans each document right after recording and returns the original, and it takes cash, checks and credit cards. Mail-in filers need a cover letter, a self-addressed stamped envelope and a check. The state deed fee is $1.85 per $500 of value, made up of $1.30 for the state and $0.55 for the county.

Transfers that are exempt include a deed given to a lender in lieu of foreclosure and a corrective deed that confirms title already held. The Register of Deeds cannot give legal advice and recommends consulting a legal professional when preparing a deed.

sections.h2: What do Mauldin sellers usually face, and how does a cash sale help?
sections.html:
Sellers in Mauldin often start looking at a cash sale for one of a few reasons:

  • A house with repairs that a buyer's lender would require
  • An inherited home where the heirs live elsewhere
  • A tenant in place or a vacant rental
  • A deadline from a job change, a move or a tax bill

With a cash purchase there is no lender appraisal to pass, and you can pick a closing date. We buy houses as they are, including those that need roofs, decks or other work that the city would permit, and you can decline the offer at no cost. We cannot name a price before reviewing the property.

faqs.q: What county is Mauldin, SC in?
faqs.a: Mauldin is in Greenville County. The county assesses the property, bills the tax and records the deed through its Register of Deeds.

faqs.q: When are Greenville County property taxes due on a Mauldin house?
faqs.a: Real estate taxes are due January 15, and bills usually go out near the end of October. State law adds a 3% penalty after January 15, with more added after February 1 and March 16.

faqs.q: Does a sale change the property tax on a Mauldin home?
faqs.a: For the buyer, yes. Greenville County reassesses a qualifying sale at current market value as of December 31 of the sale year and removes the 15% cap. The buyer must apply for the 4% owner-occupied rate.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a Mauldin house?
faqs.a: At the Greenville County Register of Deeds, Suite S-2100, 301 University Ridge in Greenville. The state fee is $1.85 per $500 of value, and the office closes in-person filing at 4:30 p.m.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to fix my Mauldin house before selling?
faqs.a: Often yes, for work such as roofs, decks, additions or demolition. The City of Mauldin lists permit forms for each, and Business and Development Services can confirm what your project needs.

faqs.q: What are the main roads through Mauldin?
faqs.a: U.S. Route 276 (Main Street) runs through the center, and Interstate 385 runs along the eastern side. I-385 connects to I-85 to the north and I-185 to the south.
